rv.q: That said, there are some substantial moral and ethical questions raised in this intriguing and engaging production.
While the production delivers on much of its potential, there remains room for greater finesse in its execution to give this thought-provoking story the impact its premise promises.
There is some genuinely good work here both in the script and from the players.

More broadly, there is a sense of artificiality both to the script and to Daniel Goldman’s direction, as though the cast are reading off a list of bullet points, answering all the misgivings someone might have about preserving a Holocaust survivor’s memories.
Memoriam is a story that is so relevant, so poignant, and so beautifully told that I would defy anyone not to be moved by what has been created.

Daniel Goldman for Tangram Theatre Company, Gabriella Sills for Gabriella Sills Productions, Noga Flaishon Genre: Contemporary, Costume, Drama, Historical, Mainstream Theatre, New Writing, Short Plays, Theatre Venue: Southwark Playhouse Large Studio, Borough Festival: FringeReview UK Rachel works for a company buying memories from people, and...
Memoriam makes a compelling family drama of the genuine conundrum of how to keep history alive when the last witnesses to it are dead.
Memoriam is the definition of challenging and thought provoking theatre.

And all of a sudden what could have been a fascinating analysis of a new (albeit fictional) medium for telling the ghastly history of the Holocaust, gets lost in a mini-parable on the evils of capitalism.
The central concept is undoubtedly strong, offering plenty of food for thought, but the script doesn't always do it justice.
Daniel Goldman’s direction skilfully weaves the polemic into a warm-hearted family saga, but ultimately both are a little compromised.
There is food for thought in this finely performed, but somewhat haphazard tale.

cn.t: An ambitious sci-fi premise about extracting Holocaust memories divides critics: some praise its thought-provoking exploration of memory and trauma, while others find the dystopian tech elements muddy the family drama at its core.
